transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because everybody keeps acting like I’m the problem, like I’m just imagining things, but I’m not. My husband keeps saying I need to “talk to somebody,” and people at the warehouse are looking at me like I’m crazy, but they know what they’re doing. They’ve been watching what I do, watching my moves, and then somehow the pallet counts get changed around, and it makes me look like I messed up.

And it’s not just once, that’s what I keep trying to tell people. It’s like every time I’m trying to show I can handle more, especially with that supervisor spot coming up, something gets switched or written different, and then I’m the one who looks unreliable. So I’m here because my husband pushed it, really, but also because I need somebody to understand that I’m not making this up.
Do you believe for certain that your coworkers are deliberately trying to sabotage you?

Yes. I mean, I can’t prove it the way they keep asking me to prove it, like with a camera right there at the exact second, but I know what’s happening. I know how those pallet counts are supposed to look when I finish, and then later they’re different, and somehow it always comes back on me like I’m careless or I don’t know what I’m doing.

And it’s not random. It started being more obvious when that supervisor spot was coming up, because I’ve been trying to show I can handle more. Then all of a sudden people are watching me closer, talking different around me, acting like they don’t know what I’m talking about when I ask questions. My husband says I’m “taking it too far,” and the people at work look at me like I’m crazy, but that’s exactly what they want — to make me look unstable so I don’t get ahead.

So yes, I believe they’re doing it on purpose. I know they’ve been watching my moves and changing things to make me look bad.
Have you been hearing voices when no one is there?

Yeah… I mean, sometimes. I don’t love saying it like that because then people take it the wrong way, but yes, there have been times when nobody is right by me and I hear it.

Like at work, if I’m in the aisle by myself, or even at home when I’m folding clothes, I’ll hear a man’s voice, clear as day, say, Nicole, check it again. And I’ll look around because it sounds like somebody is standing close enough that I should be able to see them, but there’s nobody there. It’s not like a thought in my head, not like me just worrying. It sounds like a real voice, like someone said it out loud.

And that’s part of why I check things, because if I hear that, I’m not just going to ignore it, especially with everything going on. But then if I tell people that, they act like that proves I’m crazy or something, and I’m not trying to have that thrown back at me. But yes… sometimes I do hear that voice when no one is there.
How long have these experiences been going on?

It’s been… I’d say about eight months now. Not like every single minute of every day, but that’s when I started noticing it was more than just a weird day or people acting off.

The watching, the feeling like people were paying too much attention to what I was doing and things being changed after I’d already done them — that started around then. And the voice, the “check it again” thing, that’s been around that same amount of time too. At first I tried to brush it off, like maybe I was tired or stressed, but it kept happening, and then it started lining up with stuff at work, so it didn’t feel like something I could just ignore.

So… yeah. About eight months.
Aside from these concerns about being watched and sabotaged, has your ability to manage daily life gotten worse?

Yeah… I guess it has. I don’t like saying that because it makes it sound like I just can’t handle my life, and I don’t think that’s fair, but things have definitely gotten harder.

At work, they took me off the forklift, and that really bothered me because I’ve done that kind of work before and I know how to be careful. They said it was because of the counts and because my routines were slowing things down, like I was checking and rechecking and holding up the line. And then they started keeping me away from other stuff they call safety-sensitive, like anything where they think I might cause a problem if I’m distracted or taking too long. That felt humiliating, honestly, because it’s like they’re making it look like I’m the issue.

And at home… my husband says he can’t rely on me the way he used to. Like if something needs to get done, he’ll ask me, but then he’ll double-check it or just do it himself because he says I get caught up and things don’t happen on time. I still do things, I’m not just sitting around doing nothing, but it’s not like before. There’s more arguing about whether I finished something right or whether I’m taking too long.

So yes, I guess my daily life has gotten worse, especially with work and him feeling like he can’t count on me.
Have you found yourself feeling emotionally flat or less able to express feelings than you used to?

Yeah… I think so. I didn’t really notice it at first, or maybe I didn’t want to notice it, but my husband has said things like, “Are you even listening?” or “Why are you looking like that?” And I’ll be listening, sort of, but I’m just… not reacting the way I used to.

At home I mostly end up sitting there quiet, staring at the TV or scrolling on my phone, and it’s not even like I’m really enjoying what I’m watching. It’s just on. And when he tries to joke with me or get me to laugh, sometimes I know it’s supposed to be funny, but I don’t feel much come across my face. Like inside I’m kind of dull, or blank, and then he thinks I’m mad at him, but I’m not always mad. Sometimes there’s just nothing there to show.

It makes me feel bad because I wasn’t always like that. I used to laugh more, talk more, mess around with him more. Now I can be sitting right next to him and it probably looks like I’m miles away.
Before this started, were you functioning noticeably better at work and at home than you are now?

Yes… definitely. Before all this, I mean, I wasn’t perfect or anything, but I could do my job and people trusted me to do it. I was on the forklift, I could move through my shift, get my counts done, keep up with the line. Nobody was pulling me aside all the time or telling me I was slowing everybody down.

Now it’s like my supervisors don’t see me the same way. They took me off the forklift and other safety-sensitive stuff because they said my counts and the way I do my routines were holding things up. That really stung, because work is one of the places where I used to feel like I knew what I was doing.

And at home, yes, it was better before. My husband used to just ask me to do something and believe it would get done. Now he says he can’t rely on me like he used to, and he checks behind me or does things himself. So… yeah, compared to before, I’m functioning worse now.
